goal: Complete the Pi-native Assurance experience so normal Review authorization continues through one Host confirmation without command-copy or acknowledgement turns, deterministic QA exposes bounded non-authoritative progress, default tool rendering hides protocol metadata while preserving actionable failures, and scope or breaking-revision warnings require current authoritative evidence.

acceptance.assertion: The normal awaiting_user and Review-ready paths instruct the parent Agent to call request_authorization(task_id), open exactly one existing host-derived ctx.ui.confirm, and continue from its structured result without asking the user to type /imm-canary-authorize, copy a command, report command output, or reply that confirmation completed; the slash command remains a manual recovery path and all existing zero-write cancellation and authority-binding guarantees remain unchanged.

Default imm_kernel_canary and Assurance follow-up rendering presents current state, key result, and next action while hiding raw JSON, revisions, content hashes, CAS digests, capabilities, and recovered retry noise; expanded detail may show bounded acceptance and advisory information, while unresolved failures, blockers, cancellation, timeout, stale snapshots, and required user decisions remain visible and actionable.

Deterministic QA remains non-blocking and exposes bounded deduplicated ctx.ui.notify updates for start, each verifier transition, first stalled transition, and terminal outcome, including current/total, bounded acceptance id, phase, elapsed seconds when known, and deterministic hard ceiling without predictive ETA or percentage; progress never uses setStatus, setWidget, appendEntry, sendMessage, triggerTurn, persisted workflow state, or Kernel mutation.

Shared source and packaged routing guidance forbids reporting an out-of-scope or breaking Intent revision from memory alone and requires current evidence from the authoritative TaskIntent scope_hint and revision, matching Kernel projection and enrolled identity, task-scoped staged snapshot/diff excluding unrelated dirty paths, and the exact proposed path or verification-descriptor change; confirmed mismatches retain the existing breaking-revision authority path.

The successor Spec explicitly supersedes only the prior short-QA visibility assumption, source and packaged contracts remain synchronized, no Kernel reducer, persistence, freshness, Review Bundle, semantic-neighborhood, or workload-budget behavior changes, TypeScript remains diagnostic-free, git diff is cleanly formatted, and the full repository regression passes.
